results.name: Persona-Story Alignment
results.reasoning: All user stories correctly match their personas: encryption/key rotation/CLI config/backend config → Cloud Infrastructure Admin, tenant isolation OPA → Cloud Provider Admin, IdP secret management → Tenant Admin, credential retrieval → Tenant User; no internal system stories exist.
quotes: As a Cloud Infrastructure Admin, I want secrets encrypted at rest
As a Cloud Provider Admin, I want OPA policies to enforce tenant isolation
As a Tenant User, I want to retrieve secrets

results.name: In Scope / Out of Scope Accuracy
results.reasoning: The generated document has significant In Scope and Out of Scope inaccuracies: it omits many gold-standard In Scope items (e.g., specific service applicability BMaaS/CaaS/VMaaS/MaaS/Enclave, self-service secret creation, automatic secret creation during provisioning, tenant-scoped privilege isolation, installation prerequisites, E2E testing, documentation), incorrectly places 'External secret manager integration (HashiCorp Vault)' as Out of Scope when the gold standard requires Vault-compatible store as a prerequisite (In Scope), and adds scope-creep items like 'OPA-based access control,' 'CLI configuration for encryption key settings,' and 'Secret payloads excluded from list responses' not present in the gold standard.
quotes: Installation — cloud provider must deploy and configure a Vault-compatible secret store as a prerequisite
E2E testing — secret CRUD, automatic secret creation during provisioning
External secret manager integration (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) — deferred as a future enhancement

results.name: Design Leakage
results.reasoning: The generated document contains some internal implementation details that don't belong in a PRD, specifically 'OPA-based access control' (implementation mechanism), 'OPA policies' (internal condition/mechanism), 'CLI flags' (implementation detail), and 'hub/Kubernetes-based' backend terminology (internal architecture detail), though it avoids controller names, reconciler logic, and CRD field names.
quotes: OPA-based access control enforcing tenant isolation
configure encryption key settings via CLI flags
hub/Kubernetes-based on-demand secret retrieval

results.name: Problem Statement Quality
results.reasoning: The Problem Statement describes user pain (unencrypted secrets, database exposure, no uniform retrieval, no key rotation) and cost of inaction without introducing solution language or describing how the feature works.
quotes: stored as unencrypted fields scattered across resource database tables
OSAC cannot meet basic security expectations for credential storage
every service that handles secrets must implement its own ad-hoc retrieval pattern

results.name: Async Status Visibility
results.reasoning: Neither the In Scope section nor the User Stories address async status visibility — there is no mention of users being able to see current state or failure reasons for secret creation/provisioning.
quotes: A dedicated secret resource with full CRUD operations
As a Tenant User, I want to retrieve secrets such as cluster kubeconfigs

results.name: Content Completeness
results.reasoning: The generated document covers core concepts (encryption at rest, pluggable backends, uniform secret API, tenant isolation) but misses several substantive requirements from the gold standard: automatic secret creation during resource provisioning, RBAC-based access control for secrets, self-service secret CRUD (update/delete/list with metadata), E2E testing requirements, documentation requirements, UI explicitly out of scope, and the Vault-compatible store as a prerequisite dependency.

Tenant Admin, I want to control which users can access secrets through RBAC
